content.overview: Section 188 requires board consent, and member approval by resolution where thresholds or the listed-company rule apply, for specified contracts with a related party.
content.glance: Section 188 requires board consent, and member approval by resolution where thresholds or the listed-company rule apply, for specified contracts with a related party.
content.study: Related party is defined in s. 2(76). Covered contracts include sale, purchase or supply of goods or materials, selling or buying property, leasing, availing or rendering services, appointment of an agent, appointment to an office or place of profit, and underwriting. Consent of the board at a meeting is required. A member resolution is required for a company that crosses the prescribed capital or transaction thresholds, and listed companies need the member approval the section states. A related member does not vote on the resolution, subject to the later relaxation for a transaction that is not with that member. Arm's length transactions in the ordinary course are exempt from the member-approval limb as the section provides. Disclosure in the board report is required. A contract in breach is voidable at the option of the board or shareholders as stated, and a director or employee who contracted without consent must indemnify the company.

examples.title: Office of profit
examples.body: Appointing a director's relative to a place of profit above the prescribed monthly figure needs the s. 188 route.

examples.title: Ordinary course
examples.body: An arm's length sale in the ordinary course can fall outside the member-approval requirement; the board and audit-committee duties may still apply.

distinctions: Section 188 is the contract list. Section 184 is disclosure of interest. Section 177 is audit-committee approval. SEBI LODR adds listed-company rules and is not a substitute for s. 188.

misconceptions.correction: Section 188 requires board consent, and member approval by resolution where thresholds or the listed-company rule apply, for specified contracts with a related party.

questionsAndAnswers.question: May an interested shareholder vote to approve the related-party contract?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The related member is barred from voting, subject to the proviso where the transaction is not with that member.
